faqs.q: How long does orthodontic treatment usually take?
faqs.a: Treatment typically takes 12–24 months, but the duration depends on the severity of the malocclusion, treatment method, and how consistently the patient follows instructions.

faqs.q: Why are retainers important after orthodontic treatment?
faqs.a: Teeth can naturally shift after treatment. Retainers help maintain the corrected tooth positions and reduce the risk of orthodontic relapse.

faqs.q: Can a tooth become infected again after root canal treatment?
faqs.a: Yes. Reinfection can occur due to untreated canals, leakage, new decay, cracks, or inadequate restoration. Proper cleaning, sealing, and final restoration are essential for long-term success.

faqs.q: How do I know whether I need veneers or crowns?
faqs.a: Veneers may be suitable for improving tooth shape, color, and minor aesthetic imperfections when sufficient healthy enamel remains. Crowns are generally considered when a tooth is significantly weakened or structurally compromised.

faqs.q: What are the options for replacing missing teeth?
faqs.a: Depending on the number and condition of missing teeth, options may include dental implants, implant-supported bridges, conventional bridges, or removable dentures.
